angle: Unlike other tails and p-value treatments that formalize hypotheses, this one stages a single clinical-trial story where a 0.03 one-sided versus 0.06 two-sided split motivates a 10,000-test simulation showing that peeking at the data inflates false positives from 5% to 8%.
angle_detail: Start with [01:52]–[02:38] to fix what each tail choice hypothesizes, then jump to [05:08]–[06:02] for the peeking-inflates-errors demo, which is the part worth your time. Do not expect a worked test statistic or table lookup here: both p-values arrive pre-made and every example ends in always-two-sided, so pair this with a source that shows a legitimate one-sided case. It is brisk at seven minutes with no notation clashes, so watch it for decision discipline, not computation.
